summary: Klamath County, OR: 1932 cabin, then a steel tower built 1933; gone by 1965; four footings and a step recorded in a 2022 visit.

facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1965; a 2022 visitor's photos show footings and a step near the summit

access.note: Roads run almost to the top; the last quarter mile is an abandoned road. Fallen trees could block access before that stretch. No closure or gate is mentioned in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Roads go almost to the top except the last quarter mile; fallen trees could block access before the abandoned final stretch, and wet roads could be impassable.

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com both list the tower at 60 feet (18.3 m). The current 15.2 m equals 50 feet, the height a June 1933 newspaper gave for the tower under construction.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com name the Winema National Forest; the Forest Lookouts page names the Fremont National Forest. The story reports both.

The register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say 60 feet; a June 1933 newspaper describes a 50-foot tower under construction; a 1953 survey description gives about 135 feet. The story uses 60 feet and flags the other figures.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 15.2 m appears to be the 50-foot planned height; three sources give 60 feet, so the correction is proposed. Height and forest conflicts are flagged in the story. Today's condition rests on one 2022 visitor's photo captions on WillhiteWeb, not an agency statement. The access level public is inferred from road descriptions and the absence of any closure notice; confirm with the forest before treating it as settled. The 1932 occupancy line is a newspaper plan, not a confirmed staffing record.
